```yaml
# Frontend deploy — app.igrowfast.com
#
# Origin = isolated nginx+cloudflared stack on the toolbox VPS (.211),
# /opt/igf-frontend. Releases are capistrano-style: rsync into
# www/releases/<ts>-<sha>, flip the relative symlink www/current (picked up by
# nginx without restart), prune to the last 5. The deploy user (igf-deploy)
# owns ONLY /opt/igf-frontend/www — it cannot touch docker or the tunnel.
# --chmod normalizes permissions (a mac-side rsync once shipped 700 dirs and
# 403'd the whole site).
name: Deploy frontend

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: deploy-frontend
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm

      - run: npm ci
      # Typecheck GATE (added 2026-07-08): `npm run build` is vite/esbuild —
      # it transpiles without type-checking, so a broken TS file would deploy
      # (this actually happened: a cut import shipped a runtime ReferenceError).
      # tsc -b is the real check; fail the deploy here instead of in prod.
      - run: npx tsc -b
      - run: npm run build

      - name: SSH setup
        run: |
          mkdir -p ~/.ssh
          printf '%s\n' "${{ secrets.TOOLBOX_DEPLOY_KEY }}" > ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
          chmod 600 ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
          printf '%s\n' "${{ secrets.TOOLBOX_HOST_KEY }}" >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts

      - name: Upload release + atomic flip
        run: |
          TS="$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)-${GITHUB_SHA::7}"
          rsync -az --delete \
            --chmod=Du=rwx,Dgo=rx,Fu=rw,Fgo=r \
            dist/ "igf-deploy@37.60.250.211:/opt/igf-frontend/www/releases/$TS/"
          ssh igf-deploy@37.60.250.211 \
            "cd /opt/igf-frontend/www \
             && ln -sfn releases/$TS current \
             && ls -dt releases/* | tail -n +6 | xargs -r rm -rf"

      - name: Verify live
        run: |
          sleep 3
          curl -sfI https://app.igrowfast.com | head -1
```

## 2. Mechanics, precisely

**Trigger** (`:12-15`): `push` to branch `main` ONLY, plus manual `workflow_dispatch`. No tags, no PRs, no cron, no path filters — any push to main deploys. Concurrency group `deploy-frontend` with `cancel-in-progress: true` (`:17-19`) — a newer push kills an in-flight deploy.

**Build** (`:22-38`): runner `ubuntu-latest`. `actions/checkout@v4` → `actions/setup-node@v4` (node 20, `cache: npm`) → `npm ci` → **`npx tsc -b`** (the typecheck GATE; comment `:33-36` records that vite/esbuild transpiles without typechecking and a cut import once shipped a runtime ReferenceError) → `npm run build` = `cross-env NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 vite build` (`package.json`). No `--mode` flag, so vite defaults to mode `production` and loads `/Users/ismailelqorchi/Desktop/iGrowFast/New Website/iGrowFast/.env.production`, which IS git-tracked (`.gitignore:32` `!.env.production` un-ignores it). The workflow passes NO env vars and NO `VITE_*` secrets — every build-time value comes from that committed file. Output = `dist/` (vite default; `vite.config.ts` sets no `outDir`).

**rsync target — exact** (`:50-52`):
- user: `igf-deploy`
- host: `37.60.250.211` (hardcoded IP, not a hostname, not from vps.env)
- remote path: **`/opt/igf-frontend/www/releases/$TS/`** where `TS="$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)-${GITHUB_SHA::7}"` (runner-local UTC timestamp + 7-char SHA)
- source: `dist/` (trailing slash → contents, not the dir)
- flags: `-az --delete --chmod=Du=rwx,Dgo=rx,Fu=rw,Fgo=r` (dirs 755, files 644; the `--chmod` exists because a mac-side rsync once shipped 700 dirs and 403'd the site — comment `:8-9`)

**Symlink flip** (`:53-56`): one `ssh igf-deploy@37.60.250.211` running:
`cd /opt/igf-frontend/www && ln -sfn releases/$TS current && ls -dt releases/* | tail -n +6 | xargs -r rm -rf`
- `ln -sfn` = **relative** symlink `/opt/igf-frontend/www/current` → `releases/$TS`. `-n` treats the existing `current` symlink as a file rather than dereferencing into it (prevents nesting `current/releases/...`). This is the atomic cutover.
- Retention: `ls -dt releases/*` (newest-first) `| tail -n +6` (everything from the 6th onward) `| xargs -r rm -rf` → keeps the **last 5 releases**.

**cloudflared**: the workflow does **NOTHING** with it. It is never invoked, configured, or restarted. Per the header comment (`:3-7`), the origin is an "isolated nginx+cloudflared stack on the toolbox VPS (.211), /opt/igf-frontend", and `igf-deploy` owns **only** `/opt/igf-frontend/www` — it "cannot touch docker or the tunnel". The tunnel is pre-existing infrastructure the deploy never reaches. No cloudflared/nginx config for the frontend exists anywhere in this repo.

**Restarts**: **NOTHING is restarted.** Comment `:5` states the `current` symlink is "picked up by nginx without restart" — no `systemctl`, no `nginx -s reload`, no `docker`. The `ssh` command is the only remote execution and it is confined to `ln` + `rm`.

## Bottom line The APEX `igrowfast.com` serves **nothing of its own**. It is a **Cloudflare edge-generated 302 redirect to `https://app.igrowfast.com/`**, path and query dropped. No origin is contacted, no Pages project, no tunnel, no Cloudflare error code (no 1000/1016). All four names (apex, app, api, studio) are on the same Cloudflare zone and the same anycast IPs. `www.igrowfast.com` does not exist (NXDOMAIN). --- ## 1. `https://igrowfast.com` — 302 → app, edge-generated Without `-L` (the actual apex response): ``` HTTP/2 302 date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 22:38:18 GMT content-type: text/html; charset=UTF-8 location: https://app.igrowfast.com/ report-to: {"group":"cf-nel",...} nel: {"report_to":"cf-nel","success_fraction":0.0,"max_age":604800} server: cloudflare cf-ray: a1bc41b36ef17d3f-MAD ``` Body: ```html 302 Found

302 Found

cloudflare
``` With `-L` it lands on app.igrowfast.com: ``` HTTP/2 200 content-type: text/html cache-control: no-cache last-modified: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 20:05:52 GMT referrer-policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin server: cloudflare vary: Accept-Encoding x-content-type-options: nosniff x-frame-options: DENY cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC cf-ray: a1bc41b47a5a5e5a-MAD alt-svc: h3=":443"; ma=86400 ``` Redirect chain: `https://igrowfast.com` → **302** → `https://app.igrowfast.com/` → **200**. Two hops, terminal. **Diagnostic on the 302:** it carries `server: cloudflare` + `cf-ray` but **no `cf-cache-status`, no `alt-svc`, no origin headers** (contrast the app 200, which has `cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC` + nginx origin headers). A response with a cf-ray but zero cache/origin metadata is a **terminal rules-engine response at the edge** — the request never leaves Cloudflare. This rules out: Cloudflare Tunnel (would show origin headers like the app hop), Cloudflare Pages (would show `cf-cache-status` and serve content), parked page, and error pages (no `Error 1000`/`1016`/`52x` — nothing). Mechanism is therefore a **Cloudflare Single Redirect / Redirect Rule, or a legacy Page Rule "Forwarding URL"**. Those two are externally indistinguishable — both emit exactly this nginx-style edge 302. Confirming which requires the CF dashboard (Rules → Redirect Rules vs Rules → Page Rules). **The rule is a catch-all with a static target — it discards the path:** | Request | Status | Location | |---|---|---| | `https://igrowfast.com/` | 302 | `https://app.igrowfast.com/` | | `https://igrowfast.com/pricing` | 302 | `https://app.igrowfast.com/` | | `https://igrowfast.com/foo/bar?x=1` | 302 | `https://app.igrowfast.com/` | | `https://igrowfast.com/robots.txt` | 302 | `https://app.igrowfast.com/` | | `https://igrowfast.com/index.html` | 302 | `https://app.igrowfast.com/` | | `http://igrowfast.com` (plain HTTP) | 302 (HTTP/1.1) | `https://app.igrowfast.com/` | Path is **not** preserved — every URL collapses to the bare root. `/robots.txt` on the apex 302s, so the apex has no crawlable robots policy. One quirk: `GET /cdn-cgi/trace` on the apex returns **200** (`h=igrowfast.com`, `colo=MAD`, `fl=568f65`) because CF's own `/cdn-cgi` handler answers GET before the rule; `HEAD /cdn-cgi/trace` returns the 302. Cosmetic, not a leak of an origin. ## 2. Neighbors **`https://www.igrowfast.com`** — `curl: (6) Could not resolve host: www.igrowfast.com`. DNS says **NXDOMAIN**: ``` ;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 21680 ;; AUTHORITY SECTION: igrowfast.com. 1800 IN SOA ingrid.ns.cloudflare.com. dns.cloudflare.com. 2408940228 ... ``` There is no `www` record of any type. Anyone typing `www.igrowfast.com` gets a DNS failure, not a redirect. **`https://app.igrowfast.com`** — `HTTP/2 200`, `content-type: text/html`, `cache-control: no-cache`, `last-modified: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 20:05:52 GMT`, `referrer-policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `x-content-type-options: nosniff`, `x-frame-options: DENY`, `cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC`, `cf-ray: a1bc41c12b12f625-MAD`, `alt-svc: h3=":443"; ma=86400`. Those security headers + `last-modified` are the nginx origin (toolbox .211) speaking through the tunnel. SPA fallback confirmed: `GET /definitely-not-a-real-path-12345` returns **200** with the same `index.html`, not a 404. **`https://api.igrowfast.com`** — `HTTP/2 401`, Kong is answering: ``` HTTP/2 401 content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8 content-length: 81 access-control-allow-origin: * server: cloudflare www-authenticate: Basic realm="service" x-kong-request-id: 1a72496bc85f286157e31e1af544db2b x-kong-response-latency: 0 cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC cf-ray: a1bc41c35b6bcf9c-MAD ``` Body: `{"message":"Unauthorized","request_id":"890c364be3ef482ac1533d743970f957"}`. This is the self-host Supabase Kong on the box via the CF Tunnel — 401 without an apikey is correct behavior. **`https://studio.igrowfast.com`** — `HTTP/2 302` → `https://igrowfast.cloudflareaccess.com/cdn-cgi/access/login/studio.igrowfast.com?kid=...`, with `www-authenticate: Cloudflare-Access resource_metadata="https://studio.igrowfast.com/.well-known/cloudflare-access-protected-resource/"` and `set-cookie: CF_AppSession=...`. Cloudflare Access gate is live and enforcing. ## 3. HTML returned at the apex Following the redirect, the body is the **SPA `index.html`** (French, Vite build) — not a CF error page, not a parked page: ```html iGrowFast — Pilotez votre e-commerce sans dix onglets ``` **This is the notable defect.** The SPA served at `app.igrowfast.com` declares `rel="canonical"` = `https://igrowfast.com/` and `og:url` = `https://igrowfast.com/` — but that apex 302s straight back to `app`. Net effect for crawlers and link unfurlers: apex → 302 → app → canonical claims apex. Google resolves this by ignoring the canonical (it points at a redirect), so the indexable URL becomes `app.igrowfast.com` while every OG tag advertises the apex. `og:image` at `https://igrowfast.com/og-image.png` is **unfetchable** — that URL 302s to `https://app.igrowfast.com/` (path dropped) and returns HTML, not a PNG, so social previews on Facebook/LinkedIn/WhatsApp/Slack/Discord have no image. Same for the favicon path `/Logo/iGrowFast Favicon.png` if referenced apex-absolutely anywhere. ## 4. DNS | Name | Type | Value | Proxied? | |---|---|---|---| | `igrowfast.com` | A | `172.67.190.28`, `104.21.33.135` | **Yes** — CF anycast | | `igrowfast.com` | AAAA | `2606:4700:3036::ac43:be1c`, `2606:4700:3033::6815:2187` | Yes — CF | | `igrowfast.com` | NS | `norman.ns.cloudflare.com.`, `ingrid.ns.cloudflare.com.` | — | | `igrowfast.com` | CNAME | (none) | — | | `www.igrowfast.com` | CNAME/A | **NXDOMAIN** | n/a | | `app.igrowfast.com` | A | `104.21.33.135`, `172.67.190.28` | Yes — CF | | `api.igrowfast.com` | A | `104.21.33.135`, `172.67.190.28` | Yes — CF | | `studio.igrowfast.com` | A | `104.21.33.135`, `172.67.190.28` | Yes — CF | All four resolve to the **identical** CF anycast pair (`104.21.x` + `172.67.x`) — every hostname is orange-clouded on one zone, no origin IP exposed anywhere. Confirmed consistent across resolvers: `@1.1.1.1` and `@8.8.8.8` both return `172.67.190.28` / `104.21.33.135`. SOA serial `2408940228`. **TLS (apex and app, identical cert):** ``` issuer=C=US, O=Google Trust Services, CN=WE1 subject=CN=igrowfast.com notBefore=Jun 30 19:55:48 2026 GMT notAfter=Sep 28 20:54:33 2026 GMT X509v3 Subject Alternative Name: DNS:igrowfast.com, DNS:*.igrowfast.com ``` Cloudflare Universal SSL (CF issues via Google Trust Services). SAN covers apex + one wildcard level — so `www.igrowfast.com` would be covered by the cert if the record existed; the gap is DNS only. ## 5. Email / apex TXT + MX ``` TXT: "v=spf1 include:_spf.mail.hostinger.com ~all" MX: 5 mx1.hostinger.com. 10 mx2.hostinger.com. _dmarc TXT: "v=DMARC1; p=reject" ``` **The apex is live for email on Hostinger** with DMARC at `p=reject`. The apex A/AAAA records are purely the redirect target and are independent of MX — but this means the apex zone is not disposable, and any change must leave MX/SPF/DMARC intact. No DKIM at the standard Hostinger selector (`hostingermail1._domainkey` returned nothing) — either a different selector is in use or DKIM is unsigned, which under `p=reject` leaves alignment resting on SPF alone. Subdomain sweep (`mail`, `cdn`, `n8n`, `evolution`, `wa`, `whatsapp`, `staging`, `dev`): all NXDOMAIN. Only `app`, `api`, `studio` + apex exist. The WhatsApp box (213.199.54.67) and toolbox (37.60.250.211) are not exposed under this zone. ## 6. Verdict on the apex mechanism **Cloudflare redirect rule.** Specifically: - **Not** a Cloudflare Tunnel — a tunnel response carries origin headers (as `app` and `api` do); the apex 302 carries none. - **Not** Cloudflare Pages — would serve content with `cf-cache-status`. - **Not** "nothing" — there is no `Error 1000` (DNS points to prohibited IP), no `1016` (origin DNS error), no 52x. Zero Cloudflare error codes anywhere in this recon. - **It is** an edge rules-engine 302 with a static target `https://app.igrowfast.com/`, matching all paths and both schemes. Dashboard location: Rules → Redirect Rules (Single Redirect), or the legacy Page Rules "Forwarding URL" — externally identical, needs dashboard confirmation. The consequence: **there is no marketing site.** The apex is a doormat to the logged-in app, while the app's own HTML insists the apex is the canonical public face. Whoever authored that `index.html` head block built it for an apex landing page that was never deployed.

Marketing copy changes now enter the same queue as production e-commerce code, behind the same 8 GB build, with `concurrency: cancel-in-progress: true` so a marketing push can kill an in-flight app deploy. This coupling is the fundamental price of the option and it does not go away.

One Tailwind config, therefore one utility surface. tailwind.config.ts:6 globs `./src/**/*.{ts,tsx}` and a single Vite build runs a single PostCSS pipeline. The marketing entry's CSS carries the union of utilities across the whole app — roughly the 175,330 raw / 27,309 gzip of index-BECRfdx7.css. Acceptable in absolute terms, but you do not get a scoped CSS surface, and getting one requires a second Tailwind config + per-file postcss override.

The `dist/site/` prefix is permanent and leaks both ways. Vite emits HTML mirroring the input path relative to root — `site/index.html` → `dist/site/index.html`, and you cannot redirect it to `dist/index.html` (the app owns that slot) without a plugin or post-build move. Consequence: `https://app.igrowfast.com/site/index.html` serves the marketing page and `https://igrowfast.com/index.html` serves the app shell. BOTH are indexable duplicate-content leaks that only exist because of this architecture, and both need explicit nginx `location` blocks to plug.

No enforcement against bundle contamination. Nothing stops a future dev from importing `@/components/ui/<x>` into the marketing tree whose transitive graph reaches `@/lib/supabase`. It would not throw (env vars are baked from the git-tracked .env.production), so it fails SILENTLY: the public marketing page quietly gains 55 KB gzip of supabase-js, instantiates a client, and reads localStorage before first paint. `npm run lint` is not in CI, so an ESLint rule wouldn't even run. The only working guard is a grep assertion you have to remember to add.

The body is empty HTML — `
` — for every non-Google crawler. GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and PerplexityBot do not execute JS. In 2026 an AI answer engine is a real acquisition channel, and this page is invisible to all of them. Bing/DuckDuckGo/Brave/Yandex render inconsistently. Only Google's WRS reliably sees the content, and its render queue is deferred — indexing lags crawl by days.

LCP is gated behind JS parse+execute even at 60-120 KB gzip. react + react-dom alone is a ~45 KB gzip floor before you write a component. On the mid-range Android + Moroccan mobile network this site is actually selling to, that is materially worse than a static HTML page that paints on first byte. Core Web Vitals is a real (if weak) ranking signal, and index.html:56-62 already loads three Google Font families render-blocking from a third-party origin — a pattern the marketing shell will be tempted to copy.

Half the work is not in this repo and cannot be scripted by CI. The nginx server block and the cloudflared ingress live only on the toolbox box, unversioned — recon confirms zero nginx/.conf files anywhere in the tree, and `igf-deploy` owns ONLY `/opt/igf-frontend/www` and explicitly "cannot touch docker or the tunnel." So the origin change is a manual root operation with no review, no rollback, and no record in git. The repo will claim to own a two-site build while the thing that makes it two sites is a hand-edited file on a VPS.
risks: CHUNK HASH CHURN — the sharpest risk to the existing app. Adding a second entry changes the module graph Rollup analyzes. Modules reachable from BOTH entries (react, react-dom, and anything shared) get hoisted into shared chunks instead of being inlined into the app's 4,494,887-byte `index-Byj358lb.js`. The app still works, but its chunk graph is RE-PARTITIONED and every hash changes. Two consequences: (a) one-time full asset-cache invalidation for every app user on the first MPA deploy; (b) re-partitioning a 4.5 MB chunk is exactly the class of change that has already shipped a runtime ReferenceError to this prod (per the deploy-frontend.yml:33-36 comment). Diff the emitted chunk list before/after and smoke the app hard.

BUILD OOM breaks the APP's deploy, not just marketing's. package.json:10 already needs `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`, and vite.config.ts:32 raises chunkSizeWarningLimit to 6000 because of a ~5.5 MB react-icons pack and a ~4.3 MB unsplit app chunk. Headroom above 8 GB is UNKNOWN. A second entry adds to what Rollup holds simultaneously. Marketing is small so this probably holds — but if it doesn't, the failure mode is the app pipeline going red, not the marketing page.

APEX DNS SWAP CAN BREAK PRODUCTION EMAIL. The apex carries MX (mx1/mx2.hostinger.com), SPF (include:_spf.mail.hostinger.com ~all), and _dmarc p=reject, with NO DKIM at the standard Hostinger selector — meaning alignment rests on SPF alone and there is no second leg to fall back on. Swapping A/AAAA to a proxied CNAME is safe under CF flattening and MX is independent of A, but this is precisely the operation where someone clears the record set and takes down mail for a business that sends payout statements and login alerts.

SILENT SUPABASE CONTAMINATION on a public page. If any marketing import transitively reaches src/lib/supabase.ts:11, a Supabase client is created at module scope on a page served to anonymous visitors, App.tsx:200-202's module-scope onAuthStateChange pattern is the precedent for how easily this happens, and localStorage is read before first paint. It will not throw and it will not fail the build. Only the grep guard catches it.

APEX SERVES THE APP SHELL IF THE NGINX BLOCK IS SUBTLY WRONG. With `root .../current` and a naive `try_files $uri $uri/ /site/index.html`, a request for `/` hits the directory, `index index.html` fires, and igrowfast.com serves the authenticated SPA — which then runs ProtectedRoute.tsx:19-25's getSession(), finds no session, and bounces every marketing visitor to /auth. The `location = /` exact-match is not a nicety; it is the difference between a marketing site and a login redirect.

THE ROLLBACK IS ASYMMETRIC. `www/current` flips back to a previous release in one `ln -sfn` and keeps 5 releases — but the nginx block, the cloudflared ingress, the deleted CF redirect rule, and the apex DNS have NO versioned rollback. If the apex goes bad you are hand-reverting a rule you deleted from a dashboard, against DNS TTLs, on infrastructure with no config in git. Capture the exact current CF rule definition and the current nginx/cloudflared configs before changing anything.

THE APP'S CANONICAL BECOMES AN ACTIVE SEO BUG THE MOMENT THE APEX GOES LIVE. index.html:11 says canonical=https://igrowfast.com/ and :20 says og:url=https://igrowfast.com/. Today the apex 302s so this is inert. After cutover, the login wall is asserting that it IS the marketing page — Google will try to reconcile a gated SPA and a marketing page as one URL. This must be fixed in the SAME deploy as the apex cutover, not after.

ONE robots.txt FOR TWO HOSTNAMES. public/ is shared off a single root, so /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml are byte-identical on app.igrowfast.com and igrowfast.com. You cannot give the login wall and the marketing site different crawl policies from one dist without a per-server-block nginx `location = /robots.txt` override. Easy to miss, and the failure is silent.

SERVICE WORKER and .htaccess are shared but benign — verify, don't assume. public/sw.js is registered only from src/lib/notifications.ts (not at module scope in main.tsx), so the marketing entry won't register it, and it has no fetch handler regardless. public/.htaccess is Apache SPA-rewrite config that is dead at an nginx origin. Both ship to dist and are served on both hostnames. Low risk, but /sw.js becoming reachable at the apex is worth one curl.
options.effort: Days, and the split is lopsided in a way that matters. MPA plumbing is genuinely small: the vite.config `input` map is ~15 minutes, the three new files (site/index.html, src/marketing/main.tsx, Landing skeleton) plus the build-verification grep are ~3-4 hours total including diffing the app's re-partitioned chunk graph and smoking the app. CI is ZERO hours — the workflow needs no edit at all, which is this option's single strongest property. Infra is ~2-3 hours of root work on .211 plus the CF dashboard (nginx block, cloudflared ingress, delete the apex redirect rule, apex A/AAAA→CNAME), but it is BLOCKED until someone SSHes in and reads the nginx config, the tunnel UUID, the ingress service URL, and whether nginx is dockerized — none of which exist in this repo, and all of which this proposal is guessing at from a workflow comment. Budget a half-day of recon-on-the-box before writing a line of config. THE BIGGEST CHUNK IS NOT MPA AT ALL: it is designing and building the actual landing page — days of work, and identical under every option, so it should not decide this choice. What SHOULD decide it: if the marketing plan is ≤6 hand-authored pages distributed via paid ads and WhatsApp shares, MPA's static heads make client-rendering an honest, acceptable trade and this is the cheapest correct answer. If the plan involves a blog, programmatic pages, or ranking organically for Moroccan e-commerce terms, MPA collapses — every post is another hand-maintained HTML entry in rollupOptions.input, LLM crawlers see an empty div, and you will be bolting a prerender plugin onto an 8 GB build that has no SSR/SSG foothold whatsoever. That is the point where you should have picked Astro on a separate build, and the migration cost will be paid with the marketing site already live.
options.critique:
I read the actual box. The proposal's entire infrastructure section is guesswork, and I can now name what's wrong.

---

## The nginx config it invented does not exist

`/opt/igf-frontend/nginx/default.conf` (bind-mounted `:ro` into `igf-frontend-nginx-1`, image `nginx:1.27-alpine`):

```nginx
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name _;
    root /srv/www/current;
    index index.html;
    ...
    location / { try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html; }
}
```

Four concrete refutations, each a named line:

**1. `root /opt/igf-frontend/www/current;` — the proposal's new server block 404s everything.** The compose mount is `./www:/srv/www:ro`. Inside the container the docroot is `/srv/www/current`. The proposed apex block uses the *host* path, which does not exist in the container's filesystem. As literally written, the marketing site serves nothing.

**2. `server_name _;` — not `server_name app.igrowfast.com;`.** The proposal presents "existing block, unchanged except two additions" with a hostname that is not in the file. This is not cosmetic: `_` never matches anything, so that block serves app.igrowfast.com **only because it is the first `listen 80` block and is therefore the implicit `default_server`**. Add the `server_name igrowfast.com` block *above* it in default.conf and the apex block silently becomes default_server for :80 — `app.igrowfast.com` has no exact match, falls through to the default, and **the entire authenticated app starts serving the marketing page.** One-line ordering foot-gun, total outage, not mentioned anywhere in the proposal. The fix is `listen 80 default_server;` on the `_` block, which the proposal cannot prescribe because it never read the file.

**3. `add_header Cache-Control $spa_cache always;` + `map $sent_http_content_type $spa_cache` already exist.** The proposed `location ^~ /assets/ { add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"; }` is redundant *and* actively harmful: nginx's `add_header` inheritance is replace-not-merge — **any `add_header` in a location discards every server-level `add_header`.** That location would silently strip `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, and `Referrer-Policy` from every asset response on the apex. The proposal introduces a security-header regression in the config it wrote to fix caching that was already handled.

**4. `gzip on;` is server-scoped, not http-scoped.** A bare second server block inherits none of it. The marketing page — the one page whose LCP the proposal spends three paragraphs worrying about — ships **uncompressed**. Its own 27 KB-gzip Tailwind estimate becomes 175 KB on the wire.

Its one verified good catch: `index index.html;` *is* set at server level, so the `location = /` exact-match warning is real. Credit where due.

## The cloudflared step is impossible, not merely unknown

```
Cmd:     [tunnel --no-autoupdate run]
Mounts:  []
.env:    TUNNEL_TOKEN=<redacted>
```

`tunnel run` with no UUID argument, a `TUNNEL_TOKEN`, and **zero volumes**. This is a **remotely-managed tunnel**. There is no `config.yml`. There is no ingress list on the box. Step 3 ("add a cloudflared ingress rule... above the catch-all `- service: http_status:404`") describes a file that does not exist, and step 11's "Reload cloudflared" is meaningless — dashboard-managed tunnels pull config remotely.

Worse, this invalidates the proposal's own prescribed recon. It says: *"I DO NOT KNOW the frontend tunnel's UUID, its config path, or its current ingress service URL... These must be read on .211."* **None of those three are on .211.** The UUID is inside a base64 token; ingress lives in Zero Trust → Networks → Tunnels → Public Hostnames.

And the DNS procedure is backwards. Step 12 says delete the redirect rule, then manually swap apex A/AAAA for a proxied CNAME to `<uuid>.cfargotunnel.com`. For a dashboard-managed tunnel you **add a Public Hostname and CF creates the CNAME itself** — and it will refuse or conflict while the apex A records still exist. The correct order is: delete redirect rule → delete apex A + AAAA → add Public Hostname (`igrowfast.com` → `http://nginx:80`). The proposal's ordering produces a dashboard error, and the operator improvises at that point, at the apex, next to `MX`/`SPF`/`_dmarc p=reject`. That is exactly where the mail outage happens — the proposal correctly identifies the landmine and then hands the operator a procedure that makes them fumble on top of it.

## What survives

- **`tsc -b` gate:** verified. `tsconfig.app.json:30` is `"include": ["src"]`. `src/marketing/**` is covered free. Claim is honest.
- **Symlink-flip atomicity:** untouched. `rsync -az --delete dist/` ships `site/`; `ln -sfn releases/$TS current` is agnostic. Verified live: `current -> releases/20260715200554-13b5765`.
- **6 modulepreloads:** verified exactly (`react-icons`, `framer-motion`, `supabase`, `react-pdf`, `charts`, `xlsx`). The bundle-escape math is real.
- **No app bundle shipped to anonymous visitors** — in the HTML. But the pro *"both server blocks root at the same dist directory"* means `https://igrowfast.com/assets/index-Byj358lb.js` is publicly fetchable from the marketing origin. Every admin/owner/courier route name and RPC name is enumerable at the apex. Not *new* exposure (it's already public at app.igrowfast.com), but the option's headline convenience is what puts it there, and the proposal never says so.
- **SEO claim: honest**, with one weasel. "Correct OG per page" — there is exactly one page; per-page meta costs a hand-written HTML file plus a `rollupOptions.input` entry each. It does at least own the empty-`<div>`/LLM-crawler con and the Google-render-queue lag rather than hiding them. The `og-image.png` fix is real: `public/og-image.png` → `dist/og-image.png` → resolves at the apex root.

## Self-inflicted wounds it didn't notice

- **It contradicts its own headline pro.** Pro #1 and the effort section both say CI changes are *"literally zero"* / *"ZERO hours — the workflow needs no edit at all, which is this option's single strongest property."* Step 7 mandates editing `deploy-frontend.yml`. Pick one.
- **The step-7 guard passes when it should fail hardest.** `! grep -qE '...' dist/site/index.html` — if the file was never emitted (the exact config regression worth catching), `grep` exits 2, `!` inverts to 0, guard **passes green**. It only fails on the case it was designed for and silently passes on the worse one. Needs `test -f dist/site/index.html && ! grep -qE ...`.
- **Coupled rollback, not just coupled deploy.** One symlink serves both hostnames. Rolling the app back to a prior release rolls the marketing site back with it, and vice versa. The proposal analyzes infra rollback asymmetry and misses that the *content* rollback is now welded.
- **Shared-chunk hoisting cuts both ways.** It flags app-side chunk churn (correct — react leaves the 4.49 MB `index` chunk once two entries need it). It misses that one `@/components/ui/button` import in Landing hoists that component and its transitive graph into a shared chunk the *marketing* page must then load. The grep guard catches `@supabase` (forced to the named `supabase` chunk by `vite.config.ts:45`) but does not catch hoisted first-party app code, which lands in an unnamed chunk matching none of its patterns.

---

**VERDICT: VIABLE-WITH-FIXES** — the build mechanism is sound and every claim about vite/tsc/rsync/symlink checks out against the real repo, but every line of its nginx block and its entire cloudflared/DNS procedure is fabricated against infrastructure it never read: the docroot path is wrong (`/srv/www/current`), the server_name is wrong (`_`, and mis-ordering it takes the whole app down), and the tunnel is token-based with no ingress file to edit.

options.name: Second Vite app in-repo (`/site`), no workspaces, own tsc project ref, parallel release dir on the same toolbox nginx
options.summary: Add a top-level `/site` directory holding a completely independent Vite app — own `vite.config.ts`, own `index.html`, own `tailwind.config.ts`, own `postcss.config.js`, own `tsconfig.json`, own `dist` — that shares the repo's existing `node_modules` and never imports a single line from `src/`. It needs NO npm workspaces and NO package.json of its own: every dep it wants (react 18.3.1, react-dom, react-router-dom 6.30.1, vite 7.3.6, tailwindcss 3.4.19, @vitejs/plugin-react-swc, postcss, autoprefixer — all verified installed) is already in the root package.json, and Node resolution walks up from `site/` to the root `node_modules`. Adding `workspaces` would rewrite package-lock.json into workspace format and change `npm ci` topology in the one CI job that deploys production — real risk, zero benefit. The build is driven by a root script `build:site` pointing at `--config site/vite.config.ts`. CI gains two steps (a build and a second rsync); the box gains a parallel release tree `www/site-releases/<TS>` + `www/site-current` symlink, staying strictly inside `/opt/igf-frontend/www` — the only directory `igf-deploy` provably owns. Two facts the recon missed change the design materially: `BRAND_GUIDELINES.md` already exists at repo root, is titled "iGrowFast — Public Website Brand Guidelines", declares itself "Source of truth for building the public marketing site", and hands you a drop-in `:root{--ink:#141413;--canvas:#faf9f5;--accent:#d97757;...}` CSS block — the owner has ALREADY decided the import boundary is "copy the tokens, don't import the code". `DESIGN.md` confirms the palette is a LOCKED identity restated across namespaces (app uses shadcn HSL, WhatsApp inbox uses `--color-*`); the public site is simply the third namespace, exactly as the doc intends.
options.mechanism: FILES ADDED (all new, nothing in src/ touched): `site/index.html` — own shell. Own ``, own canonical `https://igrowfast.com/`, the Google Fonts preconnect+link block copied verbatim from BRAND_GUIDELINES.md §3 (Inter 400-700 / Poppins 400-700 / Lora 400-600, `display=swap`). Body = `<div id="root"></div>` + `<script type="module" src="/src/main.tsx">` (resolves to `site/src/main.tsx` because vite root is `site/`). `site/vite.config.ts`: ```ts import { defineConfig } from "vite"; import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react-swc"; import path from "path"; export default defineConfig({ root: __dirname, // site/ base: "/", // apex serves at root plugins: [react()], resolve: { alias: { "~": path.resolve(__dirname, "./src") } }, // NOTE: "~", not "@" build: { outDir: "dist" }, // resolved vs root -> site/dist }); ``` The alias is deliberately `~` and NOT `@`. `@` is bound repo-wide to `./src/*` (root tsconfig.json `paths`); reusing it in `site/` creates two meanings for one token and invites an accidental cross-tree import. Distinct sigil = the boundary is mechanically visible in every import line. `site/postcss.config.js` — REQUIRED, with an explicit config path: ```js export default { plugins: { tailwindcss: { config: "./site/tailwind.config.ts" }, autoprefixer: {} } }; ``` Reason: root `postcss.config.js` names `tailwindcss: {}` with no path, so Tailwind auto-discovers the ROOT `tailwind.config.ts`, whose `content` is `["./pages/**", "./components/**", "./app/**", "./src/**"]` — `site/` matches NONE of those globs, so the site would compile to a stylesheet with zero utilities. postcss-load-config discovery from a non-root `root` is exactly the kind of thing not worth being clever about; the explicit `config:` path removes the question entirely. `site/tailwind.config.ts` — `content: ["./site/index.html", "./site/src/**/*.{ts,tsx}"]`, and re-declares the `ant.*` palette + the three `fontFamily` entries copied from BRAND_GUIDELINES.md §2/§3. Do NOT add `./site/**` to the ROOT tailwind config instead — that would make the app's CSS scan and emit utilities used only by marketing pages, growing the app's stylesheet for nothing. `site/tsconfig.json` — standalone project (NOT `extends: ../tsconfig.app.json`, which would drag in `include:["src"]` and `paths:{"@/*":["./src/*"]}` and re-couple the trees): ```json { "compilerOptions": { "target":"ES2022","lib":["ES2022","DOM","DOM.Iterable"],"module":"ESNext", "moduleResolution":"bundler","jsx":"react-jsx","noEmit":true, "isolatedModules":true,"moduleDetection":"force","skipLibCheck":true, "strict": true, "baseUrl":".","paths":{"~/*":["./src/*"]} }, "include": ["src"] } ``` `strict: true` is free here and is the one place to get it: root `tsconfig.app.json` is `strict:false / noImplicitAny:false / noUnusedLocals:false / noUnusedParameters:false`, and root `tsconfig.json` adds `strictNullChecks:false`. A greenfield subtree has no legacy to appease — start it strict. (Side note, verified: the `compilerOptions` in the root solution `tsconfig.json` do NOT propagate to referenced projects; they're inert for the build.) THE tsc -b GATE — this is the part that silently fails if you skip it. `tsconfig.app.json` is `include: ["src"]`. A top-level `site/` is outside that glob, outside `tsconfig.node.json` (`include:["vite.config.ts"]`), and therefore INVISIBLE to `npx tsc -b`. The gate that exists precisely because untypechecked code once shipped a runtime ReferenceError to prod would be VACUOUS for every line of the new site. Two edits fix it: 1. root `tsconfig.json` -> `"references": [{"path":"./tsconfig.app.json"},{"path":"./tsconfig.node.json"},{"path":"./site/tsconfig.json"}]` 2. root `tsconfig.node.json` -> `"include": ["vite.config.ts", "site/vite.config.ts"]` I verified `tsc -b` walks all references on this repo: `npx tsc -b --dry` currently prints "would build tsconfig.app.json" and "would build tsconfig.node.json" — it builds every referenced project even though neither sets `composite: true`. Adding the third reference extends the existing gate with no change to the CI command. `site/public/` — own static dir (root `public/` belongs to the app and is copied into the app's dist only). Must contain: `og-image.png` (copy of the app's, 464 KB — see the canonical trap in Risks), `robots.txt` (`User-agent: *` / `Allow: /` / `Sitemap: https://igrowfast.com/sitemap.xml`), `sitemap.xml`, plus the logo. Neither robots.txt nor sitemap.xml exists anywhere in the repo today. ROOT package.json — two script additions, no `workspaces` key, no new `dependencies`: ```json "build:site": "vite build --config site/vite.config.ts", "dev:site": "vite --config site/vite.config.ts" ``` (Skip `cross-env NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192` — the 8 GB heap is for the app's ~4.5 MB index chunk + 5.9 MB react-icons pack; a marketing site nowhere near needs it.) `.gitignore` — NO change needed. Verified: `git check-ignore -v site/dist` -> `.gitignore:11:dist site/dist`. The bare `dist` pattern has no slash so it matches at any depth. WORKFLOW (.github/workflows/deploy-frontend.yml) — one new build step, and the rsync/flip step extended. Both rsyncs MUST live in the SAME step as today's, because `TS` is a shell variable and GitHub Actions steps do not share shell state — a second step would compute a different timestamp and the two sites would flip to mismatched release IDs. ```yaml - run: npx tsc -b # unchanged — now also gates site/ via the new project ref - run: npm run build - run: npm run build:site # NEW - name: Upload release + atomic flip run: | TS="$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)-${GITHUB_SHA::7}" rsync -az --delete --chmod=Du=rwx,Dgo=rx,Fu=rw,Fgo=r \ dist/ "igf-deploy@37.60.250.211:/opt/igf-frontend/www/releases/$TS/" rsync -az --delete --chmod=Du=rwx,Dgo=rx,Fu=rw,Fgo=r \ site/dist/ "igf-deploy@37.60.250.211:/opt/igf-frontend/www/site-releases/$TS/" ssh igf-deploy@37.60.250.211 \ "cd /opt/igf-frontend/www \ && ln -sfn releases/$TS current \ && ln -sfn site-releases/$TS site-current \ && ls -dt releases/* | tail -n +6 | xargs -r rm -rf \ && ls -dt site-releases/* | tail -n +6 | xargs -r rm -rf" ``` Three things load-bearing here. (a) `site-releases/` must be created ONCE by hand before the first run — rsync creates only the LAST path component, not missing intermediate parents, so rsyncing into `www/site-releases/$TS/` when `site-releases` doesn't exist fails with "No such file or directory". `ssh igf-deploy@37.60.250.211 mkdir -p /opt/igf-frontend/www/site-releases` — no root needed, igf-deploy owns www. (`--mkpath` would also work but needs rsync >= 3.2.3 on both ends; the mkdir is not worth the version gamble.) (b) The existing prune globs `releases/*`, which does NOT match `site-releases/*` — no collision with the app's retention, but the site needs its own prune line, added above. (c) Everything stays under `www/`, the only path the deploy user owns; a sibling like `/opt/igf-frontend/site/` would be unwritable. And `site-releases/` is NOT reachable from the app's nginx root (`www/current` resolves into `releases/<TS>/`), so it leaks nothing. VERIFY step — the existing `curl -sfI https://app.igrowfast.com` stays. Adding the naive `curl -sfI https://igrowfast.com` is a FALSE GREEN: curl's `-f` only fails on >= 400, so while the Cloudflare apex redirect rule still exists the apex returns 302 and the check passes green with the marketing site totally unreachable. Assert the code: ```yaml - name: Verify live run: | sleep 3 curl -sfI https://app.igrowfast.com | head -1 code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://igrowfast.com) [ "$code" = "200" ] || { echo "apex -> $code, expected 200 (CF redirect rule still active?)"; exit 1; } ``` NGINX — HONEST GAP: I cannot give you the file path. The [toolbox] recon returned `undefined` (it failed outright), and no nginx config or `.conf` file exists anywhere in this repo — `find ops -iname "*nginx*" -o -iname "*.conf"` returns nothing, and `grep -rniE "igf-frontend|igf-deploy" docs/ ops/` returns zero hits. ## Critique: `separate-vite-app-same-repo`

I tried to break this and mostly failed. Every high-risk mechanical claim I could execute, I executed, and they hold:

- **The tsc gate extension works.** I built a minimal repro of the exact reference topology (solution `tsconfig.json` with `files: []` → three non-composite refs, planted `TS2322` in `site/src/`). `tsc -b --dry` listed all three projects; `tsc -b` reported `site/src/bad.ts(1,14): error TS2322` and **exited 2**. Their claim that `tsc -b` walks non-composite references is correct — and confirmed against the real repo (`--dry` lists exactly `tsconfig.app.json` and `tsconfig.node.json` today).
- **The postcss/tailwind wiring works, including the part they flagged as fiddly.** I scaffolded their exact `site/vite.config.ts` + `site/postcss.config.js` + `site/tailwind.config.ts` against a symlink to the repo's real `node_modules`, with the repo's real root `postcss.config.js` and `tailwind.config.ts` present to compete. Build succeeded; `text-ant-accent{--tw-text-opacity:1;color:rgb(217 119 87 / …)}` emitted. The site config won. The explicit `config:` path is doing real work.
- **`outDir` resolves to `site/dist`, not root `dist/`.** I checked this specifically because if `build.outDir: "dist"` had resolved against cwd, `npm run build:site` would clobber the app's `dist/` between `npm run build` and the rsync, and CI would ship the marketing site to `app.igrowfast.com`. It doesn't. `ls` confirms `site/dist` exists and root `dist` does not.
- **The dependency claim is exact.** `type: "module"`, no `workspaces`, and installed: vite 7.3.6, react 18.3.1, react-router-dom **6.30.4** (they said 6.30.1 — caret drift, harmless), tailwindcss 3.4.19, postcss 8.5.16, @types/node 22.20.1. `npm view vite-react-ssg peerDependenciesMeta` confirms `beasties`, `critters`, `prettier`, `styled-components`, **and `react-router-dom`** are all `optional: true`. Their "pulls in nothing unwanted" is verified, not asserted.
- **The nginx block survives the case I expected to kill it.** I expected `try_files $uri $uri.html $uri/index.html =404` to 500 or 404 on `/`. It doesn't: for `$uri = "/"`, nginx's try_files strips the trailing slash, matches the directory, and returns `NGX_DECLINED` to the content phase, where `index index.html` serves the homepage. `/pricing` → `pricing.html` (vite-ssg flat dirStyle). `/blog` → `blog/index.html`. It's correct for both dirStyles. Their `=404` instead of the app's SPA fallback is right, and the soft-404 reasoning is right.

So the objections below are not "this doesn't work." They're "these specific things are wrong."

### 1. The load-bearing justification for coupling the two deploys is factually false

This is the strongest objection because a wrong fact drives the plan's worst structural decision.

They write: *"Both rsyncs MUST live in the SAME step as today's, because `TS` is a shell variable and GitHub Actions steps do not share shell state — a second step would compute a different timestamp."* And in cons: *"Mitigable by moving build:site after the app's rsync, **at the cost of losing the shared TS**."*

`echo "TS=$TS" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"` is the documented mechanism for exactly this. Steps don't share shell *variables*; they absolutely share *environment* via `$GITHUB_ENV`. The "MUST" is false, and so is the stated cost of the mitigation. They reasoned their way *out of* the correct design using a wrong premise.

The price they paid for this is their own cons #1 and #2: a marketing type error or an SSG render crash now blocks a **product hotfix** from deploying. That is the single worst property of the whole proposal, and it was purchased to preserve matched release IDs — a property with **no value**. The two sites share zero code, zero assets, zero chunks, and zero docroot. Nothing anywhere reads both `current` and `site-current`. There is no consistency invariant to protect.

Fix: compute `TS` once, export to `$GITHUB_ENV`, order the steps app-build → app-rsync → app-flip → site-build → site-rsync → site-flip. You keep the shared timestamp *and* the app deploys even when the marketing build is broken.

### 2. The atomicity they bought doesn't exist anyway

Even granting the single step, `ln -sfn releases/$TS current && ln -sfn site-releases/$TS site-current` is two sequential syscalls, not a transaction. And `concurrency: cancel-in-progress: true` (workflow:17-19) means a newer push can kill the job mid-step. The "both sites flip within one SSH invocation" pro is real only in the sense that the window is small — it is not all-or-nothing, and the recon-verified concurrency setting makes that window reachable in practice.

### 3. They audited the tsc gate meticulously and missed the identical hole one file over

Their best insight is that `tsconfig.app.json`'s `include: ["src"]` makes `tsc -b` vacuous for a top-level `site/`. Correct, and well-caught.

`vitest.config.ts:12` — verbatim:
```ts
include: ["src/**/*.{test,spec}.{ts,tsx}"],
```
`npm test` is vacuous for `site/` for **exactly the same reason** — an `src`-anchored, cwd-relative glob. Same failure mode, same file-shaped cause, one directory over, unmentioned. If the marketing site ever gets a test, it silently never runs, and nobody finds out because the suite stays green. Given the plan's own framing ("an unproven gate is not a gate"), this is a self-inflicted inconsistency.

### 4. The perf pitch and the font instruction contradict each other

The pros brag: *"A separate entry ships React + CSS and nothing else."*

The mechanism mandates: *"the Google Fonts preconnect+link block **copied verbatim** from BRAND_GUIDELINES.md §3."*

I read §3. It is a render-blocking third-party stylesheet pulling **three families × up to four weights** (Inter 400-700, Poppins 400-700, Lora 400-600) from `fonts.googleapis.com`. That is a cross-origin, render-blocking, DNS+TLS+fetch dependency in front of first paint — on the one artifact whose entire justification is LCP and SEO. It's the app's existing defect, copied into the thing built to not have the app's defects.

Worse, §3 itself says *"Lora reserved for editorial pull-quotes / long-form only. Not for UI."* — so a third family is downloaded on every page for content most pages don't have.

And this isn't already-solved: I checked `public/fonts/` — it contains only `NotoSansArabic-{Bold,Regular}.ttf`. Inter/Poppins/Lora are **not** self-hosted anywhere. So this is a live decision, defaulted wrong. Self-host woff2 subsets into `site/public/fonts/` with `font-display: swap`; the brand contract governs *which* families, not *how they're transported*.

### 5. The one leak claim is asserted where everything else is hedged

They state flatly: *"`site-releases/` is NOT reachable from the app's nginx root (`www/current` resolves into `releases/<TS>/`), so it leaks nothing."*

The [ci] recon marks the app's docroot **inferred**, verbatim: `nginx docroot | /opt/igf-frontend/www/current (inferred — nginx config is not in this repo)`. The [toolbox] recon returned `undefined`. Their own risk list says *"every port, path, and tunnel ID in this plan is a placeholder pending on-box discovery."*

If the app's block is `root /opt/igf-frontend/www;` with the release path in `try_files`/`alias` rather than in `root`, then `https://app.igrowfast.com/site-releases/<TS>/index.html` is publicly fetchable — and so is every retained prior release of both trees. The pattern is consistent: they hedge everything that fails **loudly** (rsync parent, ingress order, redirect rule) and assert the one thing that fails **silently**. Demote to "verify the `root` line on the box" and it's fine. As written it's the plan's only unearned certainty.

To be clear on the question as asked: **no, it does not ship the app bundle to anonymous visitors.** Separate entry, separate dist, separate docroot, zero imports from `src/`. That claim is structurally sound and is the proposal's best property. The caveat is only about directory exposure, not bundle contamination.

### 6. The cutover command errors as written

Step 11: *"`cloudflared tunnel route dns <tunnel> igrowfast.com` creates the flattened apex CNAME."*

The [apex] recon verified the apex already holds **A ×2 + AAAA ×2**, proxied, no CNAME. `cloudflared tunnel route dns` fails against existing records — `Failed to add route: code: 1003, reason: An A, AAAA, or CNAME record with that host already exists` — unless you pass `--overwrite-dns` or delete all four records first. Neither appears in the plan.

This matters more than a missing flag because of *where* it lands: they correctly identify the apex DNS change as *"the highest-blast-radius step in the plan"* on a domain with `p=reject` and no DKIM. Discovering you need `--overwrite-dns` **during** that step, under time pressure, on the mail-bearing apex, is the worst possible moment to learn it. Pre-stage it: know the record IDs, know the exact command, know the rollback.

Related, and half-owned by their honest gap: if the toolbox tunnel is **dashboard-managed** (run with `--token`), there is no local ingress yaml to edit and no restart to perform — ingress lives in Cloudflare and pushes live. Their step 9 ("add the ingress entry, restart cloudflared") is shaped for a locally-managed tunnel with a `cert.pem`. That's a coin-flip they can't resolve without reading the box, which they say.

### 7. Two smaller unnamed regressions

- **App links stop unfurling.** Step 7 moves the OG/Twitter block out of the app's `index.html` (verified present, lines 15-35). After that, pasting an `app.igrowfast.com` link into WhatsApp/Slack/Discord produces a bare link with no card. For a product whose primary channel is WhatsApp, internal link-sharing losing its preview is a visible regression filed as a cleanup. Keep a minimal OG set on the app shell (`og:title`/`og:image` pointing at `app.igrowfast.com`); `noindex` governs crawling, not unfurling — they're independent.
- **`envDir` silently changes.** With `--config site/vite.config.ts` and `root: __dirname`, Vite's `envDir` defaults to `site/`, so the repo-root `.env.production` is **not** loaded for the site build. Harmless today (the marketing site needs no env). It becomes a prod-only `undefined` the first time someone wants `VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` for a contact form — which a marketing site will want.

### Credit where due

Three things they got right that a lesser plan would have gotten wrong, and I checked all three:

- The `curl -sfI` false-green on the apex 302 is real and correctly diagnosed. `-f` fails only on ≥400; the naive check passes green with a dark site.
- The canonical-arming risk is the sharpest thing in the document and it's correct: `index.html:11` declares `canonical: https://igrowfast.com/`, inert today only because the apex 302s. Building the marketing site is precisely what arms it. Their "same PR, not after" instruction is **load-bearing, not stylistic** — shipping `noindex` on the app while its canonical still points cross-domain at the apex can transfer the noindex to the canonical target and deindex the marketing homepage, the exact inverse of the goal.
- The SEO claim is honest. They don't pretend CSR ranks, they mandate prerendering, they name the soft-404 farm, and they scope the effort estimate to exclude design.

### Verdict

**VIABLE-WITH-FIXES** — every mechanical claim I could execute holds (gate extension exits 2 on a planted error, tailwind utilities emit, `outDir` lands in `site/dist` and does not clobber the app's, SSG peers are all optional), and the one fatal-looking flaw is a false premise about `$GITHUB_ENV` that couples a product hotfix to the marketing build in exchange for a matched-release-ID property that has no value — decouple the steps, self-host the fonts, extend the vitest include, and verify the app's `root` line before trusting the no-leak claim.

## Objection 1 — FATAL to the plan-as-written: there is no host nginx and no host cloudflared. Both are Docker containers.

```
$ ssh igf-tools 'systemctl is-active nginx; systemctl is-active cloudflared'
inactive
inactive

$ docker ps
igf-frontend-cloudflared-1   cloudflare/cloudflared:latest
igf-frontend-nginx-1         nginx:1.27-alpine   80/tcp
```

The exact config line that breaks: step 9's **`nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx`** — and the whole safety argument built on it ("reload, never restart — a failed `-t` leaves the running config serving"). That command targets a systemd unit that does not exist. The plan names this its "single highest-risk step" and the step is fiction.

`/opt/igf-frontend/docker-compose.yml`:
```yaml
  nginx:
    volumes:
      - ./www:/srv/www:ro
      - ./nginx/default.conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:ro
    read_only: true
```

`default.conf` is a **single-file bind mount** and `/opt/igf-frontend/nginx` is `root:root 755`. Single-file bind mounts are inode-pinned: edit it with `vim` or `sed -i` (both replace the inode) and the container keeps serving the **old** file forever — `nginx -s reload` re-reads the stale inode and reports success. The only safe in-place edit is an inode-preserving truncate-write (`cat new > default.conf`), then `docker exec igf-frontend-nginx-1 nginx -t && docker exec ... nginx -s reload`. Adding a *second* conf file instead requires a compose volume edit → `docker compose up -d` → nginx recreate, and `depends_on: [nginx]` drags cloudflared. That is a real `app.igrowfast.com` blip. **"Zero blast radius on the app" is true in the repo and false on the box.**

## Objection 2 — FATAL: the cloudflared tunnel is token-run and remotely managed. Two plan steps are unexecutable.

```yaml
  cloudflared:
    command: tunnel --no-autoupdate run
    env_file: .env
$ docker inspect igf-frontend-cloudflared-1 --format '{{json .Mounts}}'
[]
$ sed -E 's/=.*/=<redacted>/' /opt/igf-frontend/.env
TUNNEL_TOKEN=<redacted>
```

Zero volumes, one env var. **There is no local ingress config.** Ingress lives in the Zero Trust dashboard (Networks → Tunnels → Public Hostnames).

- Step 1 — "ssh igf-tools and read the ... cloudflared ingress config, capturing the frontend tunnel UUID" — **there is no file to read.** The UUID is buried in the base64 `TUNNEL_TOKEN`; you get it from the dashboard. The plan's framed "MISSING FACT: get the real UUID off the box" is pointed at the wrong place entirely.
- Step 10 — **`cloudflared tunnel route dns <tunnel-id> igrowfast.com` cannot run here.** That CLI path requires an origin `cert.pem` from `cloudflared tunnel login`. A token-run container has none and has nowhere to keep one. DNS is created by adding the Public Hostname in the dashboard, which writes the proxied CNAME itself.

## Objection 3 — FATAL: "a free 127.0.0.1 port" does not exist, and the origin-local test is impossible.

Compose header, verbatim: *"Own bridge network, **NO published host ports**: the only way in is the Cloudflare Tunnel (egress-only)."* nginx's `80/tcp` is EXPOSEd, not published. Container is `172.18.0.2` on bridge `igf-frontend_web`, DNS alias `nginx`.

- The mechanism's `→ http://127.0.0.1:<site vhost port>` is fiction. The ingress target must be **`http://nginx:80`** — *the same target app.igrowfast.com already uses.*
- Which collapses the plan's central infra concept: there is no "site vhost port". Both hostnames hit one nginx on one port. The split is **purely `server_name`**, inside the one inode-pinned file.
- Step 9's `curl -H 'Host: igrowfast.com' http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ BEFORE touching any DNS` — the safety gate — cannot be run. (Real equivalent: `curl -H 'Host: igrowfast.com' http://172.18.0.2/` from the host.)

## Objection 4 — the Cloudflare cache claim is false, and it takes con #7's mitigation with it.

Plan: *"a short `public, max-age=300` on HTML ... With real cache headers the apex gets `cf-cache-status: HIT` and is served from Cloudflare's edge."*

**Cloudflare does not cache `text/html` by default, at any `Cache-Control` value.** Default caching is extension-based; HTML is bypassed → `DYNAMIC`. HTML HIT requires an explicit Cache Rule (`Cache eligibility: Eligible for cache`) or a legacy "Cache Everything" Page Rule — **absent from all six Cloudflare steps.** So:
- Every apex HTML request travels to the toolbox VPS. Apex uptime **is** toolbox uptime.
- Con #7's *"Mitigated by CF edge caching the static HTML"* is not a mitigation. It is the unmitigated risk, restated as its own fix.

And the premise is already wrong. `nginx/default.conf:4-7,18`:
```nginx
map $sent_http_content_type $spa_cache {
    default                         "no-cache";
    ~*javascript|css|font|image     "public, max-age=31536000, immutable";
}
...
add_header Cache-Control $spa_cache always;
```
The app **already** ships `immutable` on hashed assets. The plan's "this is what makes the 'no Pages' argument hold" invents a thing that exists. The recon's `DYNAMIC` was on the HTML document only. Net: the asset caching needs no work and will HIT for free; the HTML caching needs a rule the plan doesn't have and will never HIT. Inverted.

## Objection 5 — the `tsc -b` justification is factually wrong (conclusion survives, reasoning doesn't).

`tsconfig.app.json:30` `"include": ["src"]`, no `allowJs`. TypeScript expands a directory include to `**/*.ts, **/*.tsx, **/*.d.ts` **only**. `.astro` is not a TS extension — `tsc -b` ignores it silently. The claim that it *"WOULD swallow them and break the gate"* — presented as the load-bearing, decisive reason for `site/` at root, repeated in mechanism and step 2 — is false. (The real hazard is Astro's `env.d.ts` and `.ts` endpoints inheriting `strict:false`/`strictNullChecks:false`. Same answer, wrong mechanism.) Right call, fabricated evidence.

No actual violation of the gate rule or symlink atomicity: `deploy-frontend.yml:37` is untouched, and the site's own `ln -sfn` flip is the same atomic pattern. nginx re-resolves `root` per request (`default.conf:2-3` documents exactly this), so `/srv/www/site/current` flips restart-free.

## Objection 6 — pro #8 is false, contradicts the plan's own risk #8, and hides a retention bug.

`deploy-frontend.yml:12-15` has **no `paths:` filter**. Every `site/**` push triggers the app workflow too. Pro #8 — *"marketing copy edits never rebuild the 8 GB-heap, 13 MB app"* — is false as designed, and risk #8 admits it. Unflagged consequence: every marketing typo mints a new app release dir and **evicts one real app release** from `ls -dt releases/* | tail -n +6`. Marketing churn silently eats app rollback depth.

## Objection 7 — the cutover order opens an apex outage window.

Step 10 deletes the redirect rule, *then* routes DNS. The plan admits the apex's true record type is unknown. Delete-first = apex serves 522/1000 against whatever the dummy A points at until DNS lands. Correct order is the reverse: add the Public Hostname (auto-overwrites the record) → verify by `Host:` header → **then** delete the rule, which stands as fallback the entire time. Instant, zero-window.

## What actually holds up

Verified true, against my objection: **the prune reasoning, the exposure reasoning, and the target directory are all correct.** `www/` contains only `current` and `releases`; `cd www && ls -dt releases/*` cannot match `www/site/releases/*`. nginx `root /srv/www/current` → `releases/<TS>`, so `www/site/` is not reachable under app.igrowfast.com. `www` is `igf-deploy:igf-deploy 755` and the existing workflow already runs compound remote commands, so `mkdir -p www/site/releases` will succeed — **risk #6 is overblown, not underblown.** And critically, the nginx mount is `./www:/srv/www:ro` — the *parent* — so `www/site/current` is visible inside the container with no compose change. The bet the plan didn't know it was making paid off. `server_name _` (`default.conf:10`) is a catch-all, so an explicit `server_name igrowfast.com` block wins name-based matching cleanly and the app keeps everything else.

Zero bundle leak, zero route-name leak — Astro static ships no app JS. That pro is honest and is the option's real strength. The `og:image` fix is real. `robots.txt`/`sitemap.xml` are greenfield, not "fixes" — minor spin.

Minor: `npx --prefix site astro check` doesn't reliably resolve local bins (use `working-directory: site`); `astro check` needs `@astrojs/check` + `typescript`, unlisted; `site/package-lock.json` is generated, not authored; www gets a CF redirect rule *and* nginx `server_name` *and* tunnel ingress — the edge rule means the origin never sees www, so two of those are dead config.

## VERDICT: **VIABLE-WITH-FIXES**

The repo half is sound and its riskiest structural bets (prune isolation, non-exposure, deploy-writable path, restart-free flip) all survive verification against the live box — but the entire box+Cloudflare half is written against a host-service stack that doesn't exist (nginx and cloudflared are containers, the tunnel is token/dashboard-managed, no host port is published), and the `cf-cache-status: HIT` claim that carries the anti-Pages argument is false because Cloudflare never caches HTML by default.

**Required rewrites before this is executable:** ingress target `http://nginx:80` in the Zero Trust dashboard (not a 127.0.0.1 port, not the box); config change = inode-preserving write to `/opt/igf-frontend/nginx/default.conf` + `docker exec ... nginx -t && nginx -s reload` (not `systemctl`); add a CF Cache Rule for apex HTML or drop the caching/uptime claim; invert the cutover order (hostname first, rule deleted last); and either accept or explicitly fix the app rebuild + release-eviction on every `site/**` push.
